model.name: Medical Procedure
model.purpose: Represent one source-qualified medical procedure occurrence or explicit non-performance so agents can distinguish request, preparation, performed technique, status, immediate outcome, outputs and safety links without conflating the event with its plan, subjects or consequences.
model.scope_statement: Owns occurrence identity and lineage, procedure classification, request and plan bindings, status, subject and focus references, performers, occurrence timing and location, method, site, approach, components, used and focal-item references, safety checks, deviations, immediate outcome, output and report links, complication and follow-up links, corrections, provenance, privacy, retention and interoperability. Definitions, requests, plans, appointments, tasks, encounters, consent, people, organizations, locations, devices, substances, specimens, observations, reports, conditions, adverse events, claims, audit and record masters remain external.
in_scope: Procedure occurrence profile, identity, source, subject, request and authorization bindings, status, participants, timing, location, performed meaning, resources, safety and deviations
Immediate outcome, output, report, complication, adverse-event and follow-up links, correction, provenance, privacy, retention and version-pinned projections
out_of_scope: Independent reusable procedure definition, ServiceRequest, CarePlan, Appointment, workflow Task, Encounter, Consent, Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, Device, Substance, Medication, Specimen, Observation, DiagnosticReport, Condition, AdverseEvent, Claim, Audit or Record lifecycles
Treating an order as performance, scheduling as start, completion as success, complication as proven causation, reported history as primary evidence or billing code as performed technique
Providing medical advice, authorizing or controlling real-time procedures, performing clinical actions, deciding malpractice or universally defining professional and legal duties

boundary_notes.distinction: A care plan may contain intended or performed procedure references, but owns its goals and planning lifecycle. The ledger containment relation is candidate and creates no cascade behavior.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-ACT-014 Health Care Delivery and WM-ACT-018 Encounter
boundary_notes.distinction: Care-delivery and Encounter masters own system, visit, service and participant context. The procedure occurrence binds them without absorbing their lifecycle.

boundary_notes.neighbor: ServiceRequest, Appointment, Task, Consent and Procedure Definition
boundary_notes.distinction: These masters own intent, scheduling, workflow fulfillment, authorization and reusable protocol. This event records what was actually attempted or done and the source-qualified links back.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-ACT-046 Clinical Observation / Diagnosis, DiagnosticReport and Condition
boundary_notes.distinction: Observations and reports own measured results and interpretations; Condition owns complication or diagnosis assertions. This event owns output links and only a bounded immediate outcome statement.
An external adverse-event case owns potential harm, severity, reporting and evolving causality. The procedure occurrence records a typed association without deciding causation.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Device, Medication, Substance, Biologically Derived Product and Specimen
boundary_notes.distinction: External masters own item identity and lifecycle. The occurrence records role-qualified use, manipulation, implantation, removal and specimen outputs with exact identifiers where available.

sources.title: FHIR R5 Procedure
sources.version_or_date: FHIR 5.0.0, 26 March 2023, maturity level 4 and Trial Use
sources.relevance: Defines a clinical event summary for an action performed on or for a subject, including request and parent links, event status, subject, focus, occurrence, recorder, reporter, performers, location, reason, body site, outcome, reports, complications, follow-up, focal devices and used items; it is not a real-time procedure-control record.

sources.title: FHIR R5 ServiceRequest
sources.version_or_date: FHIR 5.0.0, 26 March 2023, maturity level 4 and Trial Use
sources.relevance: Separates proposal, plan or order for a service from the Procedure or DiagnosticReport that records performance and results.

sources.title: FHIR R5 CarePlan
sources.version_or_date: FHIR 5.0.0, 26 March 2023, maturity level 2 and Trial Use
sources.relevance: Defines patient-specific care intent that may group request resources and performed activities while remaining distinct from generic protocols and the procedure occurrence.

sources.title: FHIR R5 AdverseEvent
sources.version_or_date: FHIR 5.0.0, 26 March 2023, maturity level 2 and Trial Use
sources.relevance: Defines harmful, potential or avoided adverse events with uncertain causal relationships, severity, outcome and context, preserving a boundary from the procedure occurrence and from complications asserted as conditions.

sources.title: FHIR R5 Observation
sources.relevance: Separates measured or assessed results and derived observations from the procedure that generated them and from the diagnostic report that groups them.

sources.title: openEHR Reference Model EHR Information Model
sources.relevance: Separates INSTRUCTION and ACTIVITY specifications from ACTION records of what was performed, supports ad hoc actions, performer context, timing and a standard instruction state machine across organizations.

sources.title: SNOMED CT Concept Model
sources.relevance: Defines procedure concepts and attributes for site, morphology, method, device, access, direct substance, occurrence, priority, focus, intent, recipient, approach and used substance or energy.

sources.title: SNOMED CT Procedure Modeling
sources.relevance: Defines procedure direct and indirect object attributes, combined-procedure criteria and the distinction among procedure, observable entity and evaluation procedure.

sources.title: International Classification of Health Interventions Reference Guide
sources.version_or_date: ICHI Reference Guide, current development publication accessed 6 September 2026
sources.relevance: Classifies intervention target, action and means; explains multiple actions, routine components, residual categories and extension codes while distinguishing planning from preparation.

sources.title: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist tools and resources
sources.version_or_date: WHO checklist and implementation material, 2009 with current resource page accessed 6 September 2026
sources.relevance: Supports identity, site, procedure and consent confirmation, team participation, pre-anesthesia, pre-incision and before-leaving checkpoints, and local adaptation under governance.

sources.title: Universal Protocol: Pre-procedure Verification
sources.relevance: United States accreditation profile for complementary wrong-person, wrong-site and wrong-procedure prevention, patient involvement and a final team time-out immediately before incision.

sources.title: OMOP Common Data Model v5.4
sources.organization: Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics
sources.relevance: Defines Procedure Occurrence identity, subject, provider, visit, start and end times, source values, normalized concepts and modifiers; warns that orders and performed activities may coexist and source-to-standard transformation requires explicit ETL choices.

sources.title: UDI Basics
sources.organization: United States Food and Drug Administration
sources.relevance: United States profile for device identifier, production identifier, lot, serial and expiry needed to distinguish device model identity from the specific item used, implanted, removed or manipulated.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 General Data Protection Regulation
sources.relevance: Provides purpose limitation, minimization, accuracy, security, access and correction safeguards for health and related procedure data.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Provides activity, entity, agent, attribution, delegation, derivation, revision, invalidation and generation semantics for procedure records and linked evidence.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Provides interoperable timestamps with seconds and explicit UTC relationship for scheduled, occurrence, performer, recorded, reported, ingested and knowledge times.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension owner and medical-procedure governance mandate
Patient, practitioner, organization, encounter, request, plan, consent, location, device, substance, specimen, observation, report, condition, adverse-event, audit and record registries
Approved procedure profiles, code and device releases, safety checklists, authority and validation rules
Privacy, consent, correction, disclosure, retention and agent policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint procedure occurrence, component, verification, performer, resource-use, outcome, deviation, status, revision, disclosure and event IDs; preserve every source-system and device identifier.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative source-system procedure occurrence identifier, source organization, subject binding and lineage head, never patient, code, date, encounter, invoice or claim alone.
Keep procedure definition, request, plan, appointment, workflow task, performed occurrence, observation, report, complication, adverse event and follow-up instruction distinct.
patch_rules: Extensions declare specialty, jurisdiction, terminology, safety, authority, device, lifecycle, privacy, retention and interoperability effects.
Released performance, status, outcome, resource-use and safety-check records are immutable; corrections create linked successors.
Never silently change subject, requested or performed procedure, body site, approach, performer, device, consent, time, status, outcome, complication link, access or provenance.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when identity, event boundary, subject, performed meaning, authority, status, time, safety and provenance survive.
Every exchange or classifier projection pins version, code system, profile and information-loss declaration.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system procedure occurrence identifier qualified by source organization and occurrence profile.
Governed globally resolvable procedure occurrence IRI.
Dimension UUID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish scheduled, preparation, start, stop, completion, performer, specimen, device, recorded, reported, ingested, observation and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, profile, subject and source binding, terminology and device versions, actor, event and knowledge times, status, access marking and provenance.

policies: The procedure occurrence is not a reusable Procedure Definition, ServiceRequest, CarePlan, Appointment, Task, Encounter, Consent, Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, Device, Substance, Medication, Specimen, Observation, DiagnosticReport, Condition, AdverseEvent, Claim, Audit or Record master.
Order, schedule, readiness, performance, completion, success, observation, report, complication and adverse event remain separate.
A completed status proves only that the recorded occurrence reached completion under its source, not that it succeeded or caused a later outcome.
Agents cannot authorize, start, stop, alter, diagnose, attribute harm, implant or remove a device, disclose data or dispose records outside explicit role and policy authority.

read: Resolve access purpose, occurrence profile, source, subject, request and consent bindings, performed definition, participants, times, status, resources, outcomes, reports, complications, lineage, holds and projection loss.
create: Bind stable occurrence identity, event boundary, source, subject, responsible authority, request or ad hoc basis and expected procedure before recording performance.
update: Append successor readiness checks, performance details, deviations, statuses, outcomes, links and corrections with reason, authority, expected revision, event time and knowledge time.
delete: Apply patient-safety, clinical-record, device, privacy, legal-hold and adopting-Dimension retention policy; retire or tombstone this occurrence without cascading to Patient, Encounter, Request, Device, Observation, Report, Condition, AdverseEvent or other masters, and let the external records policy execute physical disposition.

access.default_rule: Deny procedure, diagnosis, device, reproductive, mental-health, genetic, imaging and other sensitive clinical context unless a purpose-bound policy permits the minimum necessary view.
exceptions: Declared subject, guardian, care team, emergency, public-health, research, regulator, court or legally authorized access must cite authority, scope, purpose and time limit where applicable and must be logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, occurrence, operation, authority, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected fields, source revision and outcome without duplicating unnecessary clinical content.

read_order: Read Dimension clinical safety, scope-of-practice, consent, device, terminology, privacy, access, correction, records and agent policies.

Read this model and linked request, care plan, patient, encounter, consent, performer, location, device, substance, specimen, observation, report, condition, adverse-event and audit models before mutation.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
WM-ACT-049 Care Plan / Episode CONTAINS WM-ACT-047 is candidate metadata and not an approved composition edge.
Surgery, anesthesia, imaging, laboratory, rehabilitation, counseling, obstetric, dental, device, transfusion and other procedure families require specialty profiles.

FHIR R5 Procedure, ServiceRequest, CarePlan and AdverseEvent are Trial Use at varied maturity; ICHI is a current development publication and full SNOMED, OMOP and UDI interoperability requires release-pinned testing.
conflicts: Procedure definition, order, appointment, task, performed occurrence, result, report, complication and adverse event are not interchangeable.
Completed status does not establish success, benefit, absence of complications or causal attribution.
Source fidelity, normalized procedure coding, patient safety, privacy, correction rights and record retention can conflict and require attributable governance.
regional_assumptions: Consent, performer qualification, scope of practice, time-out, reporting, retention and disclosure rules depend on jurisdiction, specialty, setting and urgency.
Joint Commission and FDA sources are United States profiles; WHO safety materials are adaptable rather than complete local law.
Procedure codes, device identifiers and reimbursement classifications vary by jurisdiction and may not encode the actual technique performed.
adversarial_checks: Reject an occurrence without stable identity, event boundary, source, subject, responsible authority, status, occurrence time and lineage head.
Reject an order represented as performance, completed represented as successful, complication represented as proven causation or reported history represented as primary evidence.
Reject wrong-person, wrong-site or wrong-procedure readiness assertions without attributable verification under the applicable profile.
Reject corrections that overwrite prior performed details, device use, status, outcomes, complications, reports or authorship.
Reject autonomous authorization, procedure control, harm attribution, device manipulation, clinical action, disclosure or disposition outside explicit authority.
